item.title: Trump’s Voluntary A.I. Policing Echoes What Biden Did. But Is It Enough Today?
item.description: President Trump’s plan to let A.I. companies police themselves comes amid mounting examples that they are failing to put safeguards on the technology.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger
item.media:description: President Trump embraces Elon Musk while standing with other tech leaders outside the White House on Tuesday.

item.title: Congress Set to Leave Washington for the Midterms With No A.I. Progress
item.description: Senate Democrats blocked a measure that would encourage, but not require, states to protect consumers from power rate hikes tied to data center growth, and had no limits on A.I. use or deployment.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold and Cecilia Kang
item.media:credit: Paul Ratje for The New York Times
item.media:description: New homes encircle a park at Vista Del Norte Estates as construction progresses on the Meta artificial intelligence data center being built in northeast El Paso, Texas in July.

item.title: Who Attended Trump’s AI Luncheon, and Who Sat Where
item.description: A seating chart of the meeting illustrated growing divisions within the artificial intelligence industry and how it is viewed by the White House.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:description: Some of the biggest proponents of aggressive regulation were relegated to the far reaches of the table, which sat 34 people at the luncheon.

item.title: Panic and Heroics on FlyDubai Flight: ‘We Felt That This Was It’
item.description: A routine flight turned terrifying when a violent altercation broke out inside the cockpit and the aircraft dropped 17,000 feet in two minutes. Passengers subdued a knife-wielding attacker.
item.dc:creator: Karla Adam, Aaron Boxerman, Natan Odenheimer and Zane Irwin
item.media:description: Passengers from FlyDubai Flight 1073 at the Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, on Wednesday.

item.title: FlyDubai Flight to Israel Diverted After Clash Between Pilots: What We Know and Don’t Know
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel said one of the pilots may have been attempting to crash the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The plane landed in Saudi Arabia and all passengers were safe.
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands
item.media:description: A FlyDubai jet at Dubai International Airport on Tuesday.

item.title: Democrats Block Stock-Trading Bill, Denying the G.O.P. a Pre-Midterm Win
item.description: A Republican measure to limit, but not bar, congressional stock trading faltered in the Senate as Democrats thwarted a G.O.P. bid to show progress on an issue that has rankled voters.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: Stock trading by members of Congress has become a politically toxic issue for both parties, one that they are trying to use against each other in competitive midterm races.

item.title: Becerra and Hilton to Face Off in Televised California Governor Debate
item.description: Xavier Becerra, a Democrat who served in the Biden administration, will debate Steve Hilton, a Republican former talk show host, in what’s likely to be their only face-off before the election.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall
item.media:description: Xavier Becerra, left, and Steve Hilton will appear in their only scheduled debate on Wednesday night on CNN.

item.title: Andrea Shaw Says Vaccines Killed Her Twins. Authorities Say She Suffocated Them.
item.description: In a small Idaho town, a young mother is accused of killing her young twins. She blames the childhood vaccines they received.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Miller
item.media:description: Andrea Shaw appeared in court via video feed in July.

item.title: Fed’s Watchdog Finds No Misconduct or Illegal Activity in Costly Renovations
item.description: A new report by the Federal Reserve’s independent inspector general concluded that a nearly $2.5 billion construction project was poorly managed but made no referrals to the U.S. attorney general.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Renovations to the Federal Reserve became a flashpoint between President Trump and Jerome H. Powell before Mr. Powell stepped down as the central bank’s chair in May.

item.title: Justice Dept. Tries to Rebuke Federal Judges for Speaking to The Times
item.description: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz had warned that the administration’s actions “created a grave threat to the rule of law.” The attorney general accused him of “obvious bias.”
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz and Devlin Barrett
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Judge Patrick Schiltz said he was “acting well within the ethical rules that apply to federal judges in speaking to The New York Times.”

item.title: See How El Niño Is Washing Ashore in California
item.description: An enormous pulse of wave energy will soon reach Southern California and continue north, raising sea levels by half a foot and increasing threats from swells and tides.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong
item.media:description: A wave crashes into a sea wall protecting beachfront homes in Long Beach, Ca., where a boardwalk was damaged by Hurricane Marie.

item.title: Another Day of Pounding Rain Raises Flooding Fears in Texas
item.description: Texas had a dry summer, and rain on Wednesday could run off the arid ground like water on concrete.
item.dc:creator: Erin McCann, Jesus Jiménez, Ishani Desai and Judson Jones
item.media:description: Vehicles navigating a road after torrential rains moved through the Phoenix area on Tuesday.

item.title: Court Pauses Execution of Christa Pike, Tennessee’s Lone Woman on Death Row
item.description: Christa Pike tortured and murdered a classmate in 1995. She had been set to die on Wednesday, the first woman executed in the state in 200 years.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: Jessica Tezak for The New York Times
item.media:description: Christa Pike attended a hearing in Knox County Criminal Court in August via a video hookup.

item.title: Google Wants Hollywood to Stop Being So Afraid of Technology
item.description: 100 Zeros, a collaboration between Google and Range Media Partners, aims to give the tech giant a foothold in movies, TV and emerging forms of entertainment.
item.dc:creator: Brooks Barnes
item.media:credit: Michelle Groskopf for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jonathan Zepp, left, Google’s head of entertainment content and platforms, and Peter Micelli, chief executive of Range Media Partners, at Google offices in Los Angeles.

item.title: Legal Immigrants Lose Medicaid Coverage Under Trump’s Bill
item.description: Many immigrants without green cards will no longer be eligible for the health insurance program for low-income people.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Maddie McGarvey for The New York Times
item.media:description: Farahzad Sediqi is set to lose Medicaid, which helps cover her treatment for multiple sclerosis, a disorder of the central nervous system that can cause paralysis and seizures.

item.title: A Hasidic Jew Protested Against an Israeli Flag. He May Be Deported.
item.description: Yehonatan Ovadia, who opposed the mounting of the flag in a small New York town, belongs to a Hasidic branch that is anti-Zionist. He is now in ICE custody.
item.dc:creator: Luis Ferré-Sadurní
item.media:description: Yehonatan Ovadia, center, at a demonstration against Israel in New York this year. He is in federal immigration detention because of a protest he attended in 2023.

item.title: Salah Sarsour, Islamic Leader in Wisconsin, Can Be Deported, Judge Rules
item.description: Salah Sarsour, a vocal supporter of Palestinian rights who leads the state’s largest Islamic group, says the case is politically motivated and plans to appeal the decision.
item.dc:creator: Jacey Fortin
item.media:description: Salah Sarsour, president of the Islamic Society of Milwaukee, shortly after his release from a county jail in Indiana in June.

item.title: D.A. in Cornell Case Hopes to Speak to Accuser as He Weighs New Evidence
item.description: District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said a woman’s report to the police in 2024 saying she had been raped at a fraternity did not support a criminal case. But he said he was now reaching out to her.
item.dc:creator: Hurubie Meko
item.media:description: Matthew Van Houten, district attorney for Tompkins County, N.Y., said some new evidence is emerging in an allegation of rape at Cornell University.

item.title: Chi Phi Says It Acted Quickly in 2024 to Expel Cornell Members Named in Sexual Assault Lawsuit
item.description: The national organization of the Chi Phi fraternity at the center of a Cornell University sexual assault lawsuit explained publicly for the first time how it handled the episode.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University.

item.title: I Thought Things Had Gotten Better. The Cornell Case Breaks My Heart.
item.description: How could so little have changed?
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Weiner
item.media:credit: Photo Illustration by The New York Times

item.title: America Used to Be Cool. What Happened?
item.description: The world order is changing. So is the United States’ place in it.
item.dc:creator: Nadja Spiegelman, Euny Hong, W. David Marx and Vishakha Darbha
item.category: Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
Blank Space: A Cultural History of the Twenty-First Century (Book)

item.title: UK Believes Iran Played a Part in RAF Fairford Air Base Incident, Burnham Says
item.description: The British prime minister, Andy Burnham, said there were “strong indications” Iran played a part in the events at R.A.F. Fairford on Sunday, without providing details why.
item.dc:creator: Michael D. Shear
item.category: Royal Air Force Fairford (Gloucestershire, England, Air Base)
item.media:description: Outside the R.A.F. Fairford base in southwest England on Monday. Mr. Burnham said there was an “ongoing, complex and serious police investigation,” and that Britain was working closely with the United States.
